title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 74-76): Grothendieck is building a dictionary between 'conformal surgery' (compact Riemann surfaces with boundary, decorated by holomorphic disks) and algebraic geometry of stable curves. On the previous page he constructs, from a compact holomorphic curve X with boundary of type (g,ν) equipped with holomorphic disks, a stable curve X''. Disks are glued in, the centres of matched disks are identified (producing nodes), and the centres of the remaining disks are marked points. At each node, coming from a pair {x1,x2}, the anti-isomorphism between the two pointed disks gives a nonzero element (a basis) of the line T_{x1}⊗T_{x2} (or its dual). This is exactly the plumbing/smoothing parameter of the node: local coordinates z,w with zw=t. He calls this a 'structure of propagation' at the singular points. At the marked points one gets an admissible system of disks. This yields a functor from the groupoid of bordered disked holomorphic curves to the groupoid of stable curves with (1) propagator structures at nodes and (2) an admissible system of disks at the marked points.

This page lifts that functor to moduli 'multiplicités' (stacks, here real-analytic: the marginal note probably reads 'analytiques réelles'). The result is a morphism MDB_{g,ν} → M^{st}ND_{g,ν}.
- MDB_{g,ν} is the moduli stack of compact holomorphic surfaces of type (g,ν), 'disked' (D), with boundary (B).
- M^{st}ND_{g,ν} is the moduli of stable curves of type (g,ν), with combinatorial type locally constant, i.e. a single Deligne–Mumford stratum or a union of such. These curves carry propagator structures at the nodes (N) and an admissible system of disks (D) around the marked points.

The morphism is compatible with the canonical maps to a category of combinatorial types. These types are the 'Mumford–Deligne' or 'modular' diagrams: dual graphs of stable curves, weighted by genus at the vertices. Here they carry an extra 'toric structure' on the edges, a circle or C* torsor recording the phase or argument of the gluing parameter. The next page writes this as a commutative triangle over mdt_{g,ν}, where t stands for 'toric'. It then gives the undecorated analogue MD → M_{st}N over md_{g,ν}, now algebraic, with dimensions C^{3g-3+ν}×R^ν and C^{3g-3+ν}.

In modern terms, this is the stratification of moduli of curves with local coordinates or disks and plumbing data by decorated stable graphs. It is the moduli-theoretic backbone of the plumbing construction near the Deligne–Mumford boundary.
errors: The text is sketchy and unproved: 'on trouve sûrement un morphisme'. Representability and the real-analytic stack structure are not addressed.
On the previous page the line attached to a node is stated as T⊗T and then as T*∧T* (sic). The dual/tensor convention is unsettled, though harmless.

The phrase 'type loc. constant' leaves it unclear whether the target is a single stratum or the full moduli. The construction only really makes sense stratum-wise, or with real blow-up along the boundary.

ideas.what: Nonzero element of T_{x1}⊗T_{x2} at each node ('propagator structure'), obtained from matched disks, as the gluing datum of a nodal curve
ideas.modern_name: plumbing/smoothing parameter at a node; decorated nodes (tangent direction at nodes, real blow-up of the DM boundary)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Plumbing: classical (Bers, Fay, Kra, Wolpert). Moduli with node decorations: Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov 1995; Zwiebach (string field theory, early 1990s)

ideas.what: Morphism of moduli stacks from bordered disked Riemann surfaces to stable curves with node propagators and disks at marked points
ideas.modern_name: moduli of Riemann surfaces with boundary/local coordinates mapped to decorated DM strata (Segal/Costello-type models, the KSV moduli space with tangent rays)

ideas.what: Category of combinatorial types: Mumford–Deligne 'modular' diagrams, genus-weighted at vertices, with toric structures on edges; the moduli maps are compatible with it
ideas.modern_name: stable graphs / modular graphs (Getzler–Kapranov modular operads) with S^1 edge decorations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Mumford–Deligne stratification and the Teichmüller tower, but not this decorated-graph formalism as far as I know

ideas.what: Working with 'multiplicités modulaires' as real-analytic stacks

missed.claim: In 1983-84 Grothendieck frames the boundary of the moduli of curves via stable curves with 'propagators' at nodes, i.e. nonzero plumbing parameters in T⊗T, together with disks at marked points. These are indexed by 'modular' Mumford–Deligne graphs with torus decorations on edges. This anticipates the string-field-theory, plumbing-with-propagator picture (Zwiebach). It also anticipates the KSV moduli spaces with tangent rays at nodes and Getzler–Kapranov's modular graphs, all from about a decade later. His word 'propagateur' coincides with the physics term.
missed.quote: courbes algébriques stables ... à structure de propagateurs ... (N) et à système de disques (D) autour des pts marqués ... (diagrammes MD (Mumford-Deligne) ou "modulaires") ... à structures toriques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for an operadic or surgery viewpoint on moduli of curves that is usually credited to physics and to 1990s operad theory. It ties the Esquisse's 'Lego' Teichmüller tower to modular-operad formalism.

missed.claim: The commutative triangle over the toric combinatorial-type category mdt_{g,ν} is asserted, not constructed. Neither the stack structure of MDB nor the precise fibres are worked out.
missed.quote: on trouve sûrement un morphisme pour celles-ci
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly superseded by later work (KSV, Costello), so it is of limited present mathematical value.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a notable early formulation (1983-84) of decorated stable-graph stratifications, with 'propagators' at nodes and torus decorations on edges. It predates the KSV, Zwiebach and Getzler–Kapranov frameworks and uses strikingly similar terminology. But it is a sketch, and the underlying plumbing mathematics was classical.
transcription_corrections: Top-right marginal note: '(analytiques pilles)' is probably '(analytiques réelles)', consistent with '(réelles)' on the next page.
'à système admis[?] de disques': the interlinear word is likely 'admissible' (abbreviated 'adm.'), matching the previous page.

'(indexant par une pondération aux sommets) à structures toriques orientées aux arêtes': the reading is likely '(~~indexant par~~ une pondération aux sommets) à structures toriques aux arêtes'. 'orientées' is uncertain.
The target is written M_{st}ND_{g,ν} (st as subscript under M, with a crossed-out 'D'), consistent with the next page's 'M_{st}ND_{g,ν}'.
'munis (N)': the uncertain word after 'propagateurs' may be 'nodaux' or 'nommés'. N plausibly refers to the nodes ('nœuds').
